title: Measure First, Then Allocate: Calibrated Rollout Budgets for MCP Agents in Reinforcement Learning
abstract: arXiv:2610.28785v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Training tool-using language models requires costly interaction, yet identical rewards within a rollout group provide no group-relative learning signal. We use reward disagreement to guide harness evaluation and the allocation of rollouts for policy training in Model Context Protocol (MCP) environments. We first introduce Discord, which tests harness edits using exact paired inference and decision-preserving early stopping: only disagreeing paired outcomes favor one harness over another. This insight motivates prospective allocation in BRACE (Bank-calibrated Rollout Allocation under Correlated Episodes). BRACE combines historical task evidence, uncertainty in task success rates, and a correlated reward model to forecast mixed-reward groups before allocating generation budget. translated_title: 先测量，后分配：强化学习中MCP智能体的校准式Rollout预算分配
translated_abstract: 训练使用工具的语言模型需要高昂的交互成本，然而同一rollout组内完全相同的奖励无法提供组间相对的学习信号。我们利用奖励分歧来指导评测框架评估以及在模型上下文协议环境中策略训练的rollout分配。我们首先提出Discord，它采用精确配对推理和保持决策的提前停止来测试评测框架的修改：只有存在分歧的配对结果才能使一个评测框架优于另一个。这一洞察启发了BRACE（基于相关情景的银行校准rollout分配）中的前瞻性分配方法。BRACE结合历史任务证据、任务成功率的不确定性以及相关奖励模型，在分配生成预算之前预测混合奖励组。受控的评测框架实验支持Discord的有效性，而真实MCP实验则揭示了保留与成本之间的权衡。在三个Qwen3-VL模型规模上，BRACE超越了最强基线
tldr: 提出BRACE方法，利用奖励分歧测量与历史任务证据相结合的相关奖励模型，在分配生成预算前前瞻性预测混合奖励组，显著提升强化学习中MCP工具使用智能体的rollout预算分配效率。
en_tdlr: BRACE prospectively forecasts mixed-reward groups using reward disagreement, historical task evidence, and a correlated reward model before allocating rollout budgets, improving RL training efficiency for MCP tool-using agents across multiple model scales.
